primary_checks.name: The degree upper bound actually needed by the edge argument
reasoning: Every representative of a double coset differs by left and right integral unipotents, so its trace lies in a+d+kc(x). The number of such progression values in the two intervals [N/2,N] and [−N,−N/2] is at most N/c(x)+2. The number of distinct conjugacy classes is at most that number. Thus deg(x)≤N/c(x)+2, without requiring that all these classes be distinct.
Let M(t)=#{x:c(x)≤t}. From the supplied M(t)=O(t^2), partial summation gives sum_(c(x)≤t) 1/c(x)=O(t); for 1≤t≤N, therefore sum_(c(x)≤t)deg(x)=O(Nt).
For any B⊂X_N and any cutoff 1≤t≤N, sum_(x∈B)deg(x)≤O(Nt)+O((N/t+1)|B|). This is the estimate needed in §5.
primary_checks.result: The required one-sided estimate and the cutoff calculation are checked conditional on the stated double-coset counting asymptotic.
primary_checks.limits: This contribution does not certify the exact equality (4.6), the two-sided error claimed in Lemma 4.1, or non-isolation of X_N. In particular, isolated vertices contribute zero to these degree sums and do not obstruct this one-sided argument.

primary_checks.name: Geometric lower-degree mechanism
reasoning: For a radius-r semicircle, its hyperbolic length above height M is 2 arcosh(r/M) when r≥M. The length between heights M and 2M is bounded by 2 log(2+sqrt(3)): it increases to that value for r≤2M and decreases for r≥2M.
An axis meeting the fixed strip B has radius at least M_Γ≥1. Since r=sqrt(tr(γ)^2−4)/(2|c_γ|), this forces |c_γ|≤|tr(γ)|≤N, so the corresponding double coset is an actual neighbour.

Matrices in a fixed double coset and fixed PSL conjugacy class have at most two possible lifted traces. For each fixed lifted trace, the trace progression forces a fixed sum of left/right translation parameters, leaving a single Γ_∞-conjugation family. Hence there are at most a fixed number of translation families per edge. Each contributes O(1) strip length by the semicircle bound.
This yields length(C_y∩B)=O(deg(y)), as needed, allowing harmless absolute factors for the two possible lift signs.
primary_checks.result: The geometric constant-bound mechanism needed for Proposition 4.2 is checked.
primary_checks.limits: This is not a claim that every literal representative/sign sentence in the printed proof is exact. The argument only requires an absolute constant. Primitive axes and the stated cusp embedding remain part of the source setup.

primary_checks.name: Sparse equidistribution and its application threshold
reasoning: For a zero-mean bounded continuous φ, flow invariance replaces its integral on each closed orbit by the integral of φ_T. The length-proportion assumption gives an upper bound ε^(-1) times the full collection average of |φ_T|. First take X→∞ at fixed T using full-collection equidistribution; then T→∞ using the L1 ergodic theorem. This proves the stated positive-length-proportion implication conditionally on those two inputs.

In the modular sparse argument, the discarded discriminants have length at most O(e^(5X/6)+sqrt(ψ(X))length(C(X))/X). Dividing by length(I_X)≥ψ(X)length(C(X))/X makes these terms O(X e^(−X/6)/ψ(X))+O(ψ(X)^(-1/2)), both tending to zero.

The remaining discriminant subcollections satisfy the stated relative-length threshold for the cited Aka–Einsiedler theorem because ψ can be replaced by an increasing minorant, X≥log(D/4), and log length(C_D)≤log D for large D. The averaging step is valid once that external uniform sparse-equidistribution input is available.

At X≈2 log N, a hypothetical exceptional set of size at least a constant times N^2/(log N)^(1+κ), with κ≤1/4, has total length at least a constant times N^2/(log N)^κ. Relative to the threshold length(C(X))/X≈N^2/log N, the extra factor is of order (log N)^(1−κ)→∞. Thus the sparse theorem applies to the sets used in the corrected quantitative argument.
primary_checks.result: The internal two-limit and mass-discarding deductions are checked; the external equidistribution theorems themselves are not independently proved.
primary_checks.limits: The Aka–Einsiedler theorem, full prime-geodesic equidistribution, geodesic-flow ergodicity and class-number/counting results are declared dependencies.

primary_checks.name: Corrected quantitative edge count and exact-zero counterevidence
reasoning: Write L=log N and ρ=min(δ,1/2). Proposition 3.1 gives |L_f(x)|≤L^(1/2−δ)+O(1)=O(L^(1/2−ρ)) for neighbours of periods in the stated small-period set. The O(1) term must be retained when δ>1/2.
The real Gaussian CLT in Theorem 3.4 then gives |B_N|/|X_N|=O(L^(−ρ)+L^(−1/2))=O(L^(−ρ)), since real Gaussian small-interval mass is proportional to its radius.

Choose t=N/L^(ρ/2) in the checked one-sided degree bound. Both Nt and (N/t)|B_N| are O(N^2/L^(ρ/2)). The sparse geometric lower bound is sum_(y∈A_N)deg(y)≫|A_N|L when A_N is at least the target order; otherwise the target bound already holds.
It follows from these inputs that |A_N|=O(N^2/L^(1+ρ/2))=O(N^2/L^(1+min(δ/2,1/4))). This is weaker than the printed Theorem 5.1 for 0<δ<1/2.
For exact zeros, Proposition 3.1 gives |L_f(x)|=O(1) directly. Then |B_N|=O(N^2/L^(1/2)), the cutoff is t=N/L^(1/4), and the same argument gives |A_N^0|=O(N^2/L^(5/4)).

The passage to geodesic length uses |tr(γ)|=2 cosh(length(C_γ)/2), so N is comparable to e^(X/2). Summing the dyadic trace bounds gives O(e^X/X^(5/4)); the small-trace tail is of smaller order. Thus the exact-zero headline bound can be recovered without the invalid squared-radius step.
primary_checks.result: A genuine quantitative proof gap is isolated, and the checked zero-period argument preserves the stated headline exponent conditional on the named source inputs.
primary_checks.limits: No counterexample to the truth of Theorem 5.1 is claimed. The weaker small-period estimate and the exact-zero repair are new analytic deductions in this bounded contribution, not independent acceptance of the paper.

primary_checks.name: Qualitative density-one deduction for the cuspidal cases
reasoning: For cusp forms, the uniform O(1) comparison along an edge is negligible relative to sqrt(log N)/h(N) after replacing h by a slower positive minorant if necessary.

Weak convergence to the real or complex Gaussian, absence of an atom at zero, and tightness imply that the fraction of X_N with normalized periods below 1/h(N) or above h(N) tends to zero. This follows by comparison with fixed small/large rectangles or intervals, so it does not require an unsupported moving-window consequence of pointwise convergence.
If m_N=|B_N|/N^2→0, choose ψ(N)→∞ slowly enough that m_N ψ(N)→0. The degree upper bound with t=N/ψ(N) gives total incident edge mass o(N^2).

If the exceptional geodesics have positive proportion, their total length has positive proportion, so Theorem 4.5 and Proposition 4.2 give an edge lower bound of order N^2, a contradiction. If the source's set D_N={c(x)≤N/sqrt(log N)} is removed, its total degree is O(N^2/sqrt(log N))=o(N^2), so the contradiction remains.
Isolated X_N vertices have degree zero and are irrelevant to this edge-sum contradiction; no probability normalization of a graph transform is needed.
primary_checks.result: The qualitative cusp-form argument is coherent conditional on the source's period comparison, CLTs and equidistribution inputs.
primary_checks.limits: The Eisenstein case is excluded from this positive conclusion because its displayed normalizing factors are inconsistent in the source and require separate resolution.

auxiliary_claim_map.scope: A nonzero weight-zero level-one Hecke-Maaß cusp form; primitive closed geodesics ordered by length X; the zero-period set is O(e^X/X^(5/4)).

A finite-covolume Fuchsian group with a cusp. Either the modular weight-zero Hecke-Maaß case or y^(-k/2)f a nonzero holomorphic cusp form of positive even weight. For every h(X)→∞, the proportion with sqrt(X)/h(X)≤|P_f(C)|≤sqrt(X)h(X) tends to one.

The completed weight-zero modular Eisenstein series at s=1/2; claimed density-one scale sqrt(X)(log X)^(3/2), up to any factor h(X)→∞. Its printed CLT normalization is flagged below and not certified by this auxiliary.

Normality is claimed for a measure induced by the double-coset/conjugacy-class graph. Unweighted normality with an effective error is a separate conjecture. The general graph-measure construction is assigned to root's complementary check, not certified here.

Positive proportion of real quadratic fundamental discriminants ordered by the fundamental positive unit, with at least one nonzero central class-character twist. It does not settle Michel's question for every sufficiently large discriminant. The L-value deduction and level conditions are outside this bounded proof check.

For modular weight-zero Hecke-Maaß forms and δ>0, the claimed count of primitive conjugacy classes with N/2≤|tr|≤N and |P_f|≤(log N)^(1/2−δ) is O(N^2/(log N)^(1+min(δ,1/4))). The quantitative deduction is the principal finding below.
